summary: Coffin Mountain: Willamette NF summit lookout on a coffin-shaped ridge; 1906 platform, 1921 cupola, 1936 L-4, 1984 R-6 cabin; staffed in summer.

access.note: Public trail to a summit lookout that the Forest Service lists as currently staffed by the Detroit Ranger District; check conditions with the Detroit Ranger Station.

visit.trail_note: Hike about 2 1/2 miles from the trailhead on Forest Road 1168; the Forest Service calls it somewhat long but easy.

events.note: First lookout on the summit, a platform (NHLR). The local history site dates a crude pole structure to c.1905, and the Forest Service mentions structures back to 1905.
D-6 cupola cabin replaced the first lookout
Tom Humphreys, a former city mail carrier, took a lookout post; in a reprinted letter he reported snow 25 feet deep within thirty yards of the station
Lookout reported a fire on private land near the Calapooia River
Forest official announced new glass-enclosed stations for Rocky Top and Coffin Mountain in the Detroit district that fall
L-4 ground cabin, 14x14 feet, built after the D-6 cupola cabin
Newlywed Reed College students spent the summer on the lookout
July 31, 1984 Register-Guard item: the 1930s CCC-era cabin had extensive deterioration from exposure at 5,771 feet; it had been abandoned for a while with windows removed
Present R-6 flat-roofed cabin, 15 by 15 feet with a catwalk, completed in 1984
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on July 29, 2010
Statesman Journal article profiled a woman who had staffed the lookout for 29 years (as cited by a local lookout site)

evidence.supports: Coffin Mountain is in Linn County, Oregon, within the Willamette National Forest
evidence.quote: Linn County, Oregon

evidence.supports: The lookout takes its name from an elongated, coffin-shaped ridge it sits on
evidence.quote: This lookout rests atop an elongated coffin-shaped ridge, from which it derived its name.

evidence.supports: The first lookout was a platform built in 1906, replaced in 1921 with a D-6 cupola cabin (NHLR date)
evidence.quote: The first lookout on Coffin Mountain on the Willamette National Forest was a platform built in 1906 and replaced in 1921 with a D-6 cupola cabin.

evidence.supports: A local history site dates a crude pole structure to about 1905
evidence.quote: c.1905: A crude pole structure erected.

evidence.supports: The Forest Service mentions at least three structures dating back to 1905
evidence.quote: having been the location of at least three other lookout structures dating back to 1905.

evidence.supports: A D-6 cupola cabin replaced the first lookout in 1921, followed by an L-4 cab in 1936
evidence.quote: was replaced by a D-6 cupola cabin in 1921, followed by an L-4 cab in 1936.

evidence.supports: Humphreys wrote that snow still lay 25 feet deep less than thirty yards from the station
evidence.quote: There is snow 25 feet deep within thirty yards of the lookout station, he writes.

evidence.quote: The lookout on Coffin Mountain reported a fire in privately owned land near the Calapooia river.

corrections.proposed: remove: no source gives a tower height
corrections.why: The Forest Service page gives an elevation of 5771 ft and a 1984 build year but no tower height. 235 m (about 770 ft) is far above anything the sources support for this cabin.
The Forest Service page and the other site pages give 5,771 ft (about 1759 m). The Register's 5,595 ft (1,705 m) is the outlier.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR dates the first platform to 1906; a local history site dates a crude pole structure to c.1905, and the Forest Service mentions structures back to 1905. The story reports both without choosing.
The NHLR gives 5,595 ft while the Forest Service and most other pages give 5,771 ft. The Forest Service figure is used in the record.

notes_for_editor: Built timeline (1906/1921/1936/1984) agrees across NHLR, the Forest Service page and firelookout.com; the first-structure year (1905 vs 1906) and elevation (5,595 vs 5,771 ft) conflict. The 1967 Buck Mountain fire entry on the local history site was not used because the page does not clearly tie it to this summit. The July 31, 1984 item is credited to The Register-Guard on the weebly site. Fate of the 1936 L-4 cabin is not documented in the sources checked. The 2018 profile is cited second-hand through the Cheryl Hill page; the staffer is not named in the story. Brief height_m 235.0 is unsupported.
